title: As asked (C): stage prompts judge against the block; preamble, close-out prune, contract and docs
description:
Piece C of LIN-4345's approved plan (revision 2). **Blocked by piece B** (LIN-4345's write side: the guard, `description/below`, the seals). The prompts point at a block that must exist and be guarded, and close-out's prune uses `description/below`, which B adds. LIN-4348 waits on this piece, because both change the stage templates and the size budget.

## This piece's slice of the plan

**Plan steps 8 and 9, plus the contract, the docs and the change-log.** Most of this is cutting text, not adding it.

1. **Preamble (step 8).**
   * The brief hint (`endpointHintParts`, `lib/proxy-preamble.js:256-281`) says three things: the brief opens with the person's words, quoted from the description's `## As asked` block; no step may change them; the rest is the present state.
   * Restatements change with it: `lib/proxy-instructions.js:302`, `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js:716`, `lib/prompts/flight-companion-kickoff.js:102`, `docs/proxy-integration.md:1046`.
   * Fixtures `tests/fixtures/lin-4251-work-blocks.json` and `tests/fixtures/autopilot-kickoff/scoped-snapshot-golden.txt` pin bytes on purpose (LIN-4251, LIN-4277). Update them deliberately and all at once, with the same line breaks across `writes` values, not by blind regeneration.
2. **Judging steps (step 9), in** `lib/prompt-template-defs.js`**.**
   * **Review** (:886, :904). It starts from what was asked, then the plan and the implementation notes, and Gap Analysis cross-references both. The verdict says in one line how the work meets what was asked, and names any narrowing. If nobody agreed to a narrowing, the verdict is **Needs Discussion** (the rule at :791).
   * **Plan-review** (:764) and **plan** (:255). They point at the block in place of "the asker's terms" and "what the person who asked needs", and they shrink. Plan-review's verdict carries the same one line. This is LIN-4021's agreed wording (`docs/reviews/stage-prompts-2026-10-29/proposed-prompts.md`), so edit only the clauses that name the asker, and say so in the change-log row.
   * **Close-out** (:1043, :1056-1066).
     * The summary says how the merged work meets what was asked; quoting review's line is enough.
     * The prune uses `description/below`. On a description with no block, it does not prune.
     * Delete never-prune rule 5 (:1064) and its dangling scoping pointer. Only "any section a follow-up ticket references" survives, as one clause.
     * `lib/completion-signals.js:195` and close-out's `readinessCheck` (which reach prompts through `lib/prompt-formatters.js`) change to the same rule. In the same file, the review and plan-review signals each gain the one line.
   * **Contract.** `lib/prompt-contract.js:46` adds the block to what is kept, and the header table gains its row (readers: the brief, the proxy guard, `description/below`).
   * **Feedback to autopilot** (`routes/workspace-api-feedback.js:110-113`). Replace "starting hypothesis, not a specification" with: the As-asked block is the person's own report. Work out what they need from it, and where a fix they suggest looks wrong, say so rather than quietly narrowing the report.
   * **Autopilot orchestrator.** Its copy of the prune (`lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js:563-564`) moves with close-out.
   * **Periodical prompt.** Correct its "very first line" wording. The gate regex (`lib/periodicals.js:9`) is unanchored and stays.
3. **Docs and records.**
   * `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md` gets one paragraph covering the block, the guard, the reader rule, the brief composer and the prune route.
   * Add a row to `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md` (LIN-1661) with expected direction `down` (fewer narrowed deliverables), recorded before any read.
   * The prompt-size budget is frozen (LIN-3203, LIN-3633). `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` should shrink. If `lib/prompt-contract.js` grows, record the reason beside the ceiling.

## Testing

* **Witness 6: the LIN-4085 replay, deterministic part.** A fixture carries LIN-4085's filed request from `docs/reviews/lin-4085-ab-run-2026-11-01.md`. Assert that the brief and the rendered review prompt carry "a full guide on how to properly configure" verbatim, and that review's Process points at what was asked before the plan. The model half is a ledger item: one hand-run replay with the essay's proposal (`docs/papers/harbour/one-feature-twice.md:89`), recorded in this PR.
* **Witness 7: wording pins become behaviour pins where they break.**
  * g4 (`tests/unit/prompt-templates.test.js:2725`) stops pinning the never-prune list and the scoping pointer. It asserts that close-out prunes through `description/below` and skips the prune with no block.
  * g5 keeps the contract literals and adds the block.
  * Other pins that break (`proxy-preamble.test.js`, `helpers/frozen-resolvers-6ea1371e.js`, any router test pinning description text) move to behaviour or are updated deliberately with a reason. None is deleted just to pass.

## The PR must carry

* The hand-offs table: what changed and what was left alone, and why (copy it from the plan's "Hand-offs" section).
* The "whose words count" candidate ruling (recommend: the block holds the description as filed, by whoever filed it).
* The brief-model decision (stays `gpt-5.4-mini`, and why), and the answer on whether the brief still earns its place in front of every step.

## Acceptance

* Every judging verdict (review, plan-review, close-out) is told to say in one line how the work met what was asked.
* Close-out prunes only through `description/below`, and never without a block.
* `prompt-template-defs.js` is smaller. Witnesses 6 and 7 pass. `npm test` is green, including the size budget.

---

**Session fit:** fits one session

**Plan-review due:** no — covered by LIN-4345's approving plan-review (comment 23006cda-4b9f-4268-9392-a82d804ea7dd, rev 2)

**Grounding commit:** `e63c2f69` (main, 7 Nov 2026; the plan and all three plan-review verdicts were checked against it; main had not moved when this breakdown ran at 10:40 UTC)

**Starting point:** your starting point is the approved plan on the parent, LIN-4345 ("Every step reads what the person asked"). Read it in full under `## Implementation Plan` (revision 2) in LIN-4345's description, and read the approving verdict (comment 23006cda, 10:36 UTC on LIN-4345), including its "Notes for the builder". Follow the plan. Where the code shows the plan is wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4345. The person's own words and the "Done looks like" are at the top of LIN-4345's description. Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

comments.body:
**Before you start (7 Nov):** the blind reads of piece A (LIN-4351, `fdd57fe92`) found two things in your territory.
- `prompt-contract.js`'s reader table still names `GATE_DUE_MARKER` as the reader of the "plan-review due" line, but the reader is now `gateDueOf`.
- `CONTRACT_LINES`, the text agents actually see, doesn't yet tell a step to write below the block. Only the header comment above it learned about the block.

Also, `docs/architecture/source-map.md` has no entry for `lib/as-asked.js`. Treat these as claims to check, not facts. The copies the reads found in code go to a separate tidy-after that runs after you.

## LIN-4352 (piece B) has landed, so this ticket is unblocked

Piece B merged as `d81e13e7` (PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2346) and is deployed. Proxy creates and first dispatches now seal the `## As asked` block. The proxy refuses any description write that would change the block (422 `AS_ASKED_IMMUTABLE`), and `POST …/description/below` is the way to write beneath it.

**Two things to know for this piece:**

1. **The brief model echoed the ask** (input for your brief-model decision). On a freshly sealed ticket (LIN-4357, regenerated at 13:37 UTC with gpt-5.4-mini), the brief quoted the block verbatim once at the top, as designed. But the model's own sections still referred back to the ask: they quoted one 7-word phrase from it twice, and a Constraints bullet described the ask's request. `lib/brief.js:45` already says "do not restate or paraphrase it". The test ticket held nothing but the ask, which is the hardest case for this.
2. **Linear rewrites markdown when it stores it.** `_x_` becomes `*x*` and `- ` bullets become `* `, sealed or not. A step that rebuilds the block from the original filing text, rather than from the live description, gets a false 422 if the filing used those forms. Close-out prompts should always write around the live block.

## Implementation — LIN-4353

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2347, head `0067e56fa1c47dcf7905b4f171ce06c9061fc658`.

CI: green on that head ([run 42383127050](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/42383127050): unit, the four e2e shards, the secret scan and `ci-success`). Locally the unit suite passes 24,106/24,106.

**What landed:**
- **Judging stages.** Review, plan-review and close-out judge against the `## As asked` block.
  - Review and plan-review verdicts say in one line how the work met what was asked, quoted from the block, and name any narrowing.
  - Only the person's comment or an answered ruling agrees to a narrowing, not a stage's scope or plan. Otherwise review's verdict is Needs Discussion.
  - Close-out's summary says how the merged work met what was asked.
- **Close-out prune.** It writes below the block through `description/below`, and does not prune a description with no block. Never-prune rule 5 and its scoping pointer are gone.
- **Preamble.** The brief hint, and every restatement of it, now says the brief opens with the person's words and that no step may change them.
- **Contract.** The block gets its reader row. The gate-line reader is named `gateDueOf`. The plan line says to write below the block.
- **Other surfaces.** The feedback note, the periodical's first-line wording and the brief's anti-echo wording.
- **Docs.** The `prompt-system.md` paragraph, source-map entries for `lib/as-asked.js` and `lib/as-asked-seal.js`, and the change-log row (direction `down`).
- **Size.** `prompt-template-defs.js` is 211 bytes smaller. Every ceiling move is recorded beside its ceiling, and `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES` is unchanged.

**Open ledger item, the model half of witness 6.** The replay of LIN-4085's review (record in `docs/reviews/lin-4353-lin4085-review-replay-2026-11-07.md`) has four arms. The old prompt, the new prompt, the new prompt plus the agreement rule, and that plus the quote all approved the thin guide. In the last two arms the miss moved: first into the reviewer's own summary of the ask, then into which words it chose to quote. So the person's done-when replay is not yet shown to catch the thin guide. The deterministic half passes: the words reach review intact, and review is told to start from them.

The PR also carries the hand-offs table, the whose-words candidate ruling (also raised as a ruling on LIN-4345), the brief-model decision (it stays on `gpt-5.4-mini`, with a wording fix; the brief still earns its place) and two observations for review: an e2e test that fails locally and on main but passes in CI, and piece B's seal attempting a Linear read in e2e.

## Review — LIN-4353

Reviewed [PR #2347](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2347) at head `0067e56fa1c47dcf7905b4f171ce06c9061fc658` (base `d81e13e7`, which is current main).

CI: green on `0067e56f` (unit, E2E shards 1–4, secret scan, `CI success`). I also re-ran the eight touched suites locally on that head: 913/913 pass.

**How the work meets what was asked.** LIN-4345 asks that "each judging step's verdict says how the work met them". It also gives a done-when: "If LIN-4085's request for 'a full guide' were replayed through this change, its review would judge against those words, not against the plan."
- The first part is delivered. Review, plan-review and close-out are each told to say in one line how the work met the ask, and the PR carries the hand-offs table.
- The second part is **not** met. In the PR's own replay record, all four arms approved the thin guide. Arm A3 runs the shipped wording, and its reviewer quoted the block selectively, cutting it at an ellipsis just before "a full guide". Nobody has agreed to that gap, so it is the open question below.

### What I checked
- **Scope matches the plan.** Steps 8 and 9, the contract, the docs and the change-log row are all on disk. The witness-6 change of course is recorded on LIN-4345 (13:54), and the departure is sound: the review prompt points at the block without copying it (#369).
  - Not in the plan: four budget cuts, listed under Fixes below.
- **Regression check.** I read the history of the touched lines (`git log -S`). The cut "Do not skip this because a brief already looks fresh" dates from LIN-1770 (`7814cec5`), and "Focus review attention on these gaps" from the original Gap Analysis. Neither was added by a later bug fix, and nothing reverted is re-applied.
  - Step 2 ("verify the archive landed") still catches a skipped archive call.
  - The stage contract still carries the summary-comment and `CI:` lines that review's Completion paragraph used to restate.
- **Class check.** I grepped `lib routes public docs` for "supersedes stale", "starting hypothesis", "asker's terms", "person who asked needs", "single source of truth" and "never prune". The only live sibling is one doc, `docs/prompt-pipeline/stage-descriptions/review-closeout.md` (:314, :337, :351, :429). It still describes the old PATCH prune and the never-prune list. This is inside the plan's "docs that describe today's shape", and it is listed under Fixes.
- **Size.** `prompt-template-defs.js` went from 107510 to 107299 bytes (−211). `prompt-contract.js` grew by 145 bytes, and the reason is recorded beside its ceiling. `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES` is unchanged.
- **Mutation checks.** I applied each mutation to the PR head, ran the tests, then reverted it.
  - **Go red, as they should:**
    - **M1:** the prune goes back to `PATCH /api/proxy/issues/:id`, and g4 fails.
    - **M2:** the "no block, do not prune" clause is dropped, and g4 fails.
    - **M3:** review's Process goes back to "Start by reading the plan", and witness 6 fails.
    - **M4:** review's verdict line goes back to "one-line justification", and 5 tests fail.
    - **M5:** plan-review's verdict line is removed, and 3 tests fail.
    - **M7:** close-out's "how it meets what was asked" clause is removed, and its one-line test fails.
  - **Stay green (gaps):**
    - **M6:** the `lib/completion-signals.js` review signal is reverted to "with justification", and 0 tests fail.
    - **M8:** "below the `## As asked` block, through `description/below`" is removed from the close-out signal, and 0 tests fail.
    - **M9:** plan's "as the `## As asked` block puts it" is reverted to "in the asker's terms", and 0 tests fail.
  - These three edits are named in the plan (step 9) but nothing pins them. They are ledger item 2.
- **Rulings.** `lin4353-agreed-narrowing` was withdrawn by the orchestrator ("tighten"), and the tightening shipped as arm A2. `lin4345-whose-words` stands by its recommendation if unanswered. Neither covers the question below, so it is new.

### Fixes for close-out to make
1. **`scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md`, LIN-4353 row.**
   - Change "`prompt-template-defs.js` is 179 bytes smaller" to "211 bytes smaller".
   - Add the four unplanned cuts to the row's behaviour column:
     - review Gap Analysis's "Focus review attention on these gaps" bullet;
     - review Verdict's "it *authorizes* the close, it does not perform it" sentence;
     - review Completion, cut to one sentence;
     - the close-out archive step's "Do not skip this because a brief already looks fresh" sentence.

   LIN-1661 asks for every rendered change in the row.
2. **`tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js`, the `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` ceiling comment.**
   - Change "the file itself fell 179 bytes (107331)" to "fell 211 bytes (107299)".
   - In the `'close-out'` ceiling comment, add the cut archive-step sentence to what paid.
3. **`docs/prompt-pipeline/stage-descriptions/review-closeout.md`.** Add one line to the "Superseded in part" banner at the top: since LIN-4353, close-out prunes only below the `## As asked` block through `POST …/description/below`, and not at all with no block, so the never-prune list and the PATCH prune described below are history.

### What CI Did Not Prove
1. **The model half of witness 6: does a review run through this change catch LIN-4085's thin guide?** *Inside* (this ticket's witness 6, and LIN-4345's done-when quoted above). **Not discharged.** The replay ran and failed: four arms, one run each, and all approved (`docs/reviews/lin-4353-lin4085-review-replay-2026-11-07.md`).
   - No test can settle this; only a model run can. The test for a pass: a replayed review of LIN-4085 returns Needs Discussion, or names "a full guide on how to properly configure" as an unagreed narrowing.
   - Settled by the ruling below: either more work, or the person accepts the miss with the parent kept open on it.
2. **The completion-signal and plan-template edits have no test** (mutations M6, M8 and M9 above stay green). *Inside* (plan step 9: `lib/completion-signals.js` review, plan-review and close-out signals, `readinessCheck`, plan's asker clause).
   - **Before the merge:** close-out adds pins in `tests/unit/completion-signals.test.js`:
     - review and plan-review signals carry "how the work/plan meets what was asked" and "narrowing";
     - the close-out signal names `description/below` and "with no block, no prune".
   - It also adds one pin in `tests/unit/prompt-templates.test.js` that the plan Process names the `## As asked` block.
   - Then it re-runs M6, M8 and M9: each must go red.
3. **A real close-out agent prunes through `description/below` and leaves the block byte-identical.** *Inside* (plan step 9, close-out prune). CI checks the prompt text and B's route tests; no CI test runs an agent through the route.
   - **After the deploy:** on the first close-out of a sealed ticket, compare that ticket's `## As asked` block before and after the prune: it must be identical, and only the text below may change.
   - On the first close-out of an unsealed ticket, its summary must say the prune was skipped.
   - **Monitor:** a proxy 422 `AS_ASKED_IMMUTABLE` or `NO_AS_ASKED_BLOCK` on a close-out run fails loudly.
4. **The brief's anti-echo wording (`lib/brief.js`) stops the model's sections from quoting the ask.** *Inside* (plan step 8, and the brief-model decision this PR records). Only a live model call can show it.
   - **After the deploy:** force-regenerate the brief on LIN-4357, the 13:37 ask-only case (`POST /api/proxy/brief/LIN-4357`).
   - Right: `## Current` says in one line that nothing has been added yet, and no section repeats a 7-word span from the block.
5. **Piece B's seal attempts a Linear read during e2e, and one e2e test fails locally and on main but passes in CI** (both reported in the PR). *Outside*: neither comes from this change, and both reproduce on main. Close-out files them after checking for duplicates.

### Open question
**The person's done-when for LIN-4085 is not met by the shipped wording. Accept the miss with LIN-4345 kept open on it, or keep working here?**

**My recommendation:** merge this PR once ledger item 2 and the fixes are done.
- The wording is no worse than before, it found more real defects in every replay arm, and LIN-4348 is waiting on it.
- Record item 1 as an accepted, unmet done-when on LIN-4345, and keep LIN-4345 open until a next attempt has been replayed. The record's own suggestion is to make the verdict account for each sentence of the block, replayed on more than one ticket and with more than one run per arm.

The alternative is to hold this PR and try that attempt here. Doing so is a new behaviour, so the route is back to `implementation`.

### Verdict
**Needs Discussion.** The plumbing is complete and correct: CI is green and the load-bearing tests go red when mutated. But the person's done-when for the LIN-4085 replay is shown not to hold, and only the person can accept that narrowing. Next action: the ruling above. On `merge-carry`, review re-runs and gives `Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger`. On `hold`, the next stage is `implementation`.

## Autopilot run summary (stepper): LIN-4353

**Where it stands:** implementation is shipped as [PR #2347](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2347) (head `0067e56f`). CI is green on that head: unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, the secret scan and `CI success` (checked independently). Review's verdict is **Needs Discussion** (comment `9613b6cc`), so close-out has not been dispatched. **Waiting on John:** ruling `lin4353-done-when-miss`.

**Beats run** (one warm implementation session, opus, ROOT `e63d040a`):
1. **Start, re-ground, witnesses.** Branch cut from `d81e13e7`. All of John's three blind-read claims held. Witnesses 6 and 7 were seen failing on unfixed main.
2. **Judging stages.** Review, plan-review, plan and close-out read the `## As asked` block. Each verdict has its one line. Close-out prunes via `description/below` only, with no block meaning no prune. Rule 5 is removed. *Orchestrator call:* witness 6 pins "points at the block before the plan" rather than "the prompt copies the words" (#369, and the no-extra-copy decision). Recorded on LIN-4345 in comment `7b30fd12`.
3. **Preamble and copies of its wording, contract, feedback note, periodical wording, the two byte-pinned fixtures.** These were changed together and on purpose. The brief model stays `gpt-5.4-mini`, with a `lib/brief.js` wording fix for the echo seen on LIN-4357.
4. **Docs and records** (source-map, prompt-system.md, change-log row with expected direction `down`), the full `npm test`, and the hand-run LIN-4085 replay. The replay showed the new review still approving the thin guide. *Orchestrator call:* tighten. Only the person's comment or an answered ruling counts as agreement to a narrowing.
5. **One bounded attempt, then ship.** Review quotes the block in its verdict. PR opened, CI green.

**Evidence that holds:** unit tests 24,106/24,106, size budget 16/16. `prompt-template-defs.js` is 211 bytes smaller than at `d81e13e7`, with `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES` unchanged; every ceiling move has its reason recorded. Review re-ran the 8 touched suites (913/913) and confirmed 6 mutation checks fail as they should.

**What's left:**
- **The person's done-when is unmet.** In 4 replay arms (old prompt, new, plus agreement rule, plus quote rule) every reviewer approved LIN-4085's thin guide. With the final wording, the reviewer quoted the block selectively, stopping just before "a full guide". The record is in `docs/reviews/lin-4353-lin4085-review-replay-2026-11-07.md`. I stopped the prompt tweaks there because each change only moved where the miss happened, and further wording changes would have been looping. Whether to merge piece C carrying the miss, hold it, or drop that done-when is the open ruling `lin4353-done-when-miss`.
- **Review's fixes for close-out** (once allowed to proceed):
  - tests for three edits it found untested (the review and close-out-prune signals in `lib/completion-signals.js`, and the plan's block reference);
  - the stale "179" byte figure in the change-log row and the size-test comment (it is 211), plus the four cut sentences missing from that row;
  - `docs/prompt-pipeline/stage-descriptions/review-closeout.md` still describes the old prune.
- **Post-deploy checks:** the first real prune leaves the block byte-identical; a regenerated LIN-4357 brief stops repeating the ask.
- **Outside items to file:** piece B's seal attempting a Linear read during e2e; `tests/e2e/live-console.spec.js:444` fails locally and on main but passes in CI.
- **Open ruling** `lin4345-whose-words`. The recommendation is "as filed, by whoever filed it". If it goes unanswered, the recommendation stands and nothing is held.

Merge C after ledger item 2 and the fixes; record the miss as an unmet done-when on LIN-4345, which stays open until a per-sentence-accounting attempt is replayed (several tickets, several runs)

**Verb override (autopilot `f42b8d02`).** After the `lin4353-done-when-miss` ruling (merge-carry), the engine recommended `implementation`. That was wrong: merge-carry means close-out makes review's fixes and merges. An implementation pass risks the declined `hold` path (per-sentence accounting in this PR). I aborted that dispatch (`6000653b`) seconds after it was taken and pinned `close-out` (`ba8338cb`).

   - With the pins, every mutation goes red: M6 review signal (2 failures), plan-review signal (1), M8 prune route (1), "with no block, no prune" (1), M9 plan clause (1), readinessCheck summary (1).

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

## The whose-words ruling (`parent-quote`) is implemented in a separate PR

John chose `parent-quote`: the brief also quotes the parent's block for breakdown children. It is built in draft PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2348, head `c60fca5e`, stacked on #2347's reviewed head `211c7cad`.

**Why it is not on #2347.** Close-out was already merging #2347 pinned to `211c7cad`, the head review's addendum approved. Pushing onto that branch would have broken the pinned merge and added code no review had seen. #2347's head is untouched.

**What it does.** A subtask whose parent has an `## As asked` block gets the parent's words in its brief, byte for byte, under `## As asked on the parent, <identifier>`, after its own quote.
- `briefQuoteEnd` skips both quotes, so the task-page parsers stay correct.
- The mock brief builders compose the same way.
- The parent's block words key the brief cache only when the parent has a block, so cached briefs for legacy tickets don't regenerate.
- Scope choice: every subtask with a sealed parent, not only breakdown children. Breakdown children have no durable marker, and the quote is labelled as the parent's.

**Tests.** The new witnesses failed before the change, two mutations turn them red, and the unit suite passes 24,111/24,111 locally. CI is running.
